rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley are prohibited from inquiring about or using criminal history in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. They cannot refuse to rent, terminate tenancy, demand higher deposits or rent, or disqualify tenants based on criminal history, with certain exemptions.
rules.summary_plain: In Berkeley, landlords cannot ask about or use your criminal history to decide if you can rent or to treat you differently in renting, except in limited cases.
rules.summary_plain_es: En Berkeley, los propietarios no pueden preguntar ni usar su historial criminal para decidir si puede alquilar o para tratarlo de manera diferente al alquilar, excepto en casos limitados.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all rental housing providers in Berkeley except specified exemptions.
rules.exemptions_text: Exemptions include lifetime sex offenders, certain public housing/Section 8 properties, owner-occupied properties with 1-3 units where owner lives in one unit, units with rental agreements allowing owners to move back, and units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines from $1,000 to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or triple one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
